description.executive: The place where teams see the architecture working, with every result labeled so nothing is overstated.
description.l100: A web app and API that show patterns, lessons, labs and an offline demo.
description.l200: React frontend over a FastAPI control plane; routes stay thin and call services; no credentials in the browser.
description.l300: make run-api and make run-frontend; typed API contracts are generated from the backend OpenAPI document.
description.l400: Correlation IDs on every response, problem-shaped errors (404/409/422/503) and labels validated by the envelope model.

description.executive: AI coding agents that speed up data engineering while every change stays reviewable.
description.l100: Copilot (VS Code, CLI, App, cloud agent) and Claude Code read repo instructions and call MCP tools.
description.l200: Harnesses provide the agent loop and permissions; AGENTS.md, .mcp.json and .claude/skills are shared by both.
description.l300: Copilot CLI and Claude Code both load the root .mcp.json (Microsoft Learn + ffia-local) and AGENTS.md.
description.l400: Harness permissions are not authorization; writes still go through plan, approval and a scoped writer.

components.name: GitHub Copilot and Claude Code
components.offline_equivalent: Agents work against this repo and the ffia-local MCP server with no tenant.

description.executive: Microsoft-authored know-how packaged for agents, so they follow correct Fabric procedures.
description.l100: SKILL.md knowledge packs that teach an agent how to do Fabric tasks correctly.
description.l200: Skills are knowledge, not execution; they drive REST, SQL, KQL or PySpark under the user's identity.
description.l300: Installed through the Copilot CLI or Claude Code plugin marketplace; repo skills live in .claude/skills.
description.l400: The bundled MCP configuration allows broad tools; teach a hardened, read-only overlay for dev workspaces.

components.name: Fabric Skills
components.offline_equivalent: Skill procedures rehearsed against the Local Fabric Educational Provider.

description.executive: Where business reasoning, orchestration and evaluation of AI agents is run and governed.
description.l100: Hosts agents that use tools and knowledge to answer questions and propose actions.
description.l200: Owns reasoning and orchestration; consumes Fabric context; never performs authoritative writes directly.
description.l300: Arrives in Phase 6 through the Foundry project SDK and Agent Framework adapters.
description.l400: Tool calls can require approval; the Fabric data agent tool is preview and uses on-behalf-of identity.

components.name: Foundry Agent Service
components.offline_equivalent: Shown as UNAVAILABLE in the offline demo until Phase 6 adds a labeled local equivalent.

description.executive: The open-source framework teams use to build and test agents consistently.
description.l100: A library for building agents and multi-agent workflows in Python and .NET.
description.l200: Runs locally or against Foundry; supports workflows, tools and human-in-the-loop steps.
description.l300: Arrives in Phase 6 with a deterministic local client for offline tests.
description.l400: Approval-required functions pause execution until a human decision is recorded.

description.executive: A standard way for agents to reach Fabric capabilities; it does not decide who may do what.
description.l100: Several MCP servers expose Fabric docs, OneLake, items, SQL, DAX and authoring tools to agents.
description.l200: Pick the narrowest server; they run with the caller's Fabric permissions; status differs by server.
description.l300: Pinned profiles live in config/mcp/profiles.yaml; offline (Microsoft Learn + ffia-local) is the default, fabric-docs and fabric-readonly are read-only, and authoring is a separate opt-in profile.
description.l400: Do not conflate servers; pin versions; read-only allow-lists by default; writes go through the change flow.

components.name: Fabric MCP servers
components.offline_equivalent: ffia-local exposes allow-listed educational tools over synthetic data.

description.executive: A safe teaching server that shows the protocol without touching any real system.
description.l100: A local MCP server with read-only and plan-only tools over synthetic data.
description.l200: Allow-listed from config/policies/tools.yaml; no approve, execute, shell or SQL tools.
description.l300: make run-mcp, or let Copilot or Claude Code start it from .mcp.json.
description.l400: Unknown manifest tools fail fast at startup; every call is rate-limited and audited; logs go to stderr.

description.executive: One governed front door for AI models and tools, with cost and usage control.
description.l100: A gateway that sits in front of models and MCP servers.
description.l200: Adds authentication, rate limits, logging and policies in front of MCP servers and model endpoints.
description.l300: Documented reference only in this repo; no gateway is deployed.
description.l400: A gateway enforces transport policy; it does not replace per-operation authorization and approval.

components.name: API Management as AI and MCP gateway
components.offline_equivalent: Local rate limiter and audit in ffia-local.

description.executive: One governed copy of business data, refined in stages so everyone trusts the same numbers.
description.l100: Raw data becomes Bronze, then cleaned Silver, then business-ready Gold.
description.l200: Lakehouses in OneLake hold each layer; notebooks transform; tests check row counts and baselines.
description.l300: Offline, ffia data build creates Bronze, Silver and Gold Parquet for each synthetic profile.
description.l400: Idempotent writes, grain checks and reconciliation against expected baselines prove correctness.

components.name: OneLake medallion lakehouse
components.offline_equivalent: DuckDB over Parquet in the Local Fabric Educational Provider.

description.executive: The agreed business definitions, so reports and agents give the same answer.
description.l100: Tables, relationships and measures that define business meaning.
description.l200: Direct Lake reads Gold Delta tables; measures are the governed definitions agents should reuse.
description.l300: The synthetic contract lives in data/synthetic/semantic/<profile>/semantic-model.yaml.
description.l400: Measures are evaluated by name against baselines; free-form DAX is not exposed offline.

components.name: Semantic model (Direct Lake)
components.offline_equivalent: Local semantic YAML with measure evaluation.

description.executive: Lets people ask questions of governed data in plain language, within their permissions.
description.l100: A curated agent that answers questions over selected Fabric data.
description.l200: Uses the end user's identity; Fabric permissions decide what is visible.
description.l300: Called from Foundry through a preview tool or MCP endpoint (Phase 6).
description.l400: On-behalf-of only; one data agent per Foundry agent; same-region constraints apply.

components.name: Fabric data agent
components.offline_equivalent: Local deterministic answers over the semantic model.

description.executive: A shared business vocabulary across domains, still in preview.
description.l100: Business entities and relationships bound to Fabric data.
description.l200: Gives many consumers one model of the business without copying data.
description.l300: Behind preview feature flags; never required for the default demo.
description.l400: Bindings inherit item permissions; preview behavior can change.

description.executive: Keeps operational data flowing into Fabric and recoverable when something goes wrong.
description.l100: Systems drop change files into a landing zone and Fabric replicates them.
description.l200: Snapshot plus incremental files; processed files are cleaned up after seven days.
description.l300: ffia recovery run simulates snapshot, incrementals, failure, restore and replay.
description.l400: INSERT rows are not de-duplicated; upserts and deletes need keys; file names are 20-digit sequences.

description.executive: Identity decides authority, for people and for agents.
description.l100: Who you are decides what you can see and change.
description.l200: User, approver and writer are different identities; agents act on behalf of users or as scoped identities.
description.l300: Live work uses az login in a demo tenant; identifiers stay in git-ignored files.
description.l400: Least privilege, on-behalf-of for user data, managed identity for writers.

components.name: Entra identity
components.offline_equivalent: Named actors in the simulated change flow.

description.executive: The same rules applied every time, before any human is asked.
description.l100: Rules that decide whether a change is allowed and how risky it is.
description.l200: Policy files define operations, risk and rollback; overlays can narrow but not remove approval.
description.l300: config/policies/writes.yaml and tools.yaml, evaluated by policies/engine.py.
description.l400: Deterministic evaluation; unknown operations are high risk and blocked.

description.executive: An accountable person decides on high-impact changes.
description.l100: A different person approves or rejects each proposed change.
description.l200: Separation of duties, expiry and destination binding protect the decision.
description.l300: POST /api/v1/approvals; MCP has no approve tool.
description.l400: Approvals expire and are bound to a destination hash; re-execution is refused.

description.executive: Only one narrow, accountable service can actually change things.
description.l100: The service that performs an approved change and nothing else.
description.l200: Least-privilege identity bound to specific targets; LIVE writes are never redirected to LOCAL.
description.l300: Offline it writes to a simulated workspace (SIMULATED); the live writer arrives later.
description.l400: Re-checks preconditions and destination hash at execution; verifies against the system of record.

description.executive: A record of who asked, who approved and what happened.
description.l100: Every step writes an audit record you can look up.
description.l200: Records share a correlation ID across plan, approval, execution and tool calls.
description.l300: GET /api/v1/audit/<correlation_id> or the get_audit_record MCP tool.
description.l400: Redacted at write time; append-only JSONL locally; production needs an external sink.

description.executive: Measured quality instead of impressions.
description.l100: Checks answers and numbers against expected results.
description.l200: Deterministic baselines for data; model-graded evaluators for language quality.
description.l300: POST /api/v1/evaluations/run compares measures with data/synthetic/expected.
description.l400: Thresholds come from the overlay; evaluation gates the offline demo.

description.executive: Visibility into what agents did, how long it took and what it cost.
description.l100: Logs and traces that show each step.
description.l200: Structured logs with correlation IDs locally; traces in a monitoring service in production.
description.l300: Structured, redacted logs today; OpenTelemetry tracing arrives in Phase 6.
description.l400: Never log tokens; correlate spans with audit records.

description.executive: The demo and the platform degrade gracefully and say so.
description.l100: When a live service fails, reads use a labeled local copy.
description.l200: Timeouts, retries and a circuit breaker per capability; writes never fall back.
description.l300: FFIA_ENVIRONMENT=hybrid FFIA_SIMULATE_FABRIC_OUTAGE=1 shows the fallback.
description.l400: Client errors never trigger fallback; breaker states CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN.

description.executive: Lets the architecture be taught anywhere, honestly labeled as local.
description.l100: A local copy of the medallion data that works without the cloud.
description.l200: Read-only, allow-listed operations over synthetic Parquet; never presented as Fabric.
description.l300: DuckDB over Parquet built by ffia data build.
description.l400: Envelopes reject non-cloud labels that claim a cloud operation.

flows.label: Read synthetic context and propose plans
Ask governed questions on behalf of the user
Govern, limit and log tool traffic
Caller permissions decide what is allowed

layers.name: Experience and harnesses
layers.question: Who is asking, and which agent loop runs?
layers.summary: People, apps and coding agents (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code) plus the knowledge that makes them competent.

layers.name: Reasoning and orchestration
layers.question: Who thinks, plans and orchestrates?
layers.summary: Foundry agents and Agent Framework turn governed context into reasoning, plans and proposals.

layers.name: Capability access
layers.question: How are capabilities reached?
layers.summary: MCP servers and gateways standardize access. Access is not authority.

layers.name: Governed context
layers.question: Where does trusted business context live?
layers.summary: Fabric owns governed data, semantics and data agents.

layers.name: Authority
layers.question: Who may do it?
layers.summary: Entra identity, deterministic policy, human approval and a scoped writer decide what may change.

layers.name: Evidence
layers.question: How do we know what happened?
layers.summary: Audit records, evaluation and tracing turn claims into proof.

layers.name: Resilience
layers.question: What happens when a service is down?
layers.summary: A router with timeouts, retries and a circuit breaker falls back to labeled local equivalents for reads only.
